_comment: Layer 2 (candidate supply) configuration. Extends, never replaces, the Layer 1 taxonomies: role families come from config/role_taxonomy.json (applied to profile bios), skills from config/skills_taxonomy.json (applied to bios, repository metadata and READMEs), geography from config/geo.json. This file adds what Layer 1 does not need: sampling frames for the GitHub user search, the data-repository lexicon, the project topic/format/README taxonomies and the evidence-strength rules. Versioned: see 'version'.

github_search._comment: GitHub user search is token-based on the free-text location field. Each token is searched separately; the union is normalised afterwards with config/geo.json. 'frame' names: A = bio-signal (data keyword in bio, all Austrian tokens); B = complete Styrian population (all users with >=1 public repo whose location matches a Styrian token); C = base-rate sample for other regions (users with >=1 public repo, sliced by account-creation year, capped per token). Frame A runs bio keywords against 'frame_a_tokens' only (the long 'location_tokens_austria' list is used for normalisation and for Frame B/C coverage); the token 'Austria' already matches every location string containing it, e.g. 'Vienna, Austria'.

base_rate_sample._comment: Frame C: per token, users with >=1 public repository, sliced by created-year windows so that no slice exceeds the 1,000-result cap; each slice is truncated to 'per_slice_cap' results ordered by 'joined' (deterministic). This is a systematic, not random, sample: it over-represents older accounts within each window only if the window exceeds the cap.

bio_role_overrides._comment: Bios are not job titles. Before the Layer 1 title rules are applied to a bio, these patterns catch self-descriptions the title rules would miss or misread. First match wins; otherwise config/role_taxonomy.json rules run on the cleaned bio. Rules are ordered strong-role-noun first; the last rule 'ai_ml_generic' catches generic ML/AI/data wording and is ADJACENT (not a declared data role): such accounts only become data-signal candidates through repository evidence (T2).

rules.normalized: Data Governance / Data Steward / Data Manager

transition_patterns._comment: Bio wording that states a career transition or a prior domain. 'from' groups are the prior field; presence with a data role in the same bio = observed transition signal.

data_repo_lexicon._comment: A repository is classified as a data project when (a) its primary language is Jupyter Notebook or R, or (b) any keyword below matches its name, description or topics, or (c) a data topic is set. Matching is case-insensitive on word boundaries; 'exclude' patterns veto (e.g. 'database driver', 'metadata'). This is deliberately inclusive at the repo stage; project-level evidence rules are stricter (see evidence_rules). Tightened 2026-09-18 after a private precision review (bare 'data', 'ai', 'experiment', 'pipeline', 'dashboard', 'postgres', 'cv', 'stats' removed; compound forms kept).

educational_patterns._comment: Repositories that look like course work, tutorials or learning logs. They are kept but flagged; archetype = educational/tutorial.

project_topics._comment: Project themes (§15 of the brief). Matched on repository name + description + topics + README (when fetched). A project can carry several themes; 'analytics_domain' is the business domain, 'ds_method' the analytical method, 'engineering' the data-engineering component, 'ai' the GenAI component. Rule (2026-09-18): a theme counts when it matches the repository name/description/topics, or when at least two distinct patterns of the theme match the README; single generic README hits are ignored.

project_formats._comment: How a project is packaged (§16). Detected from file-tree entries (top level), primary language, homepage URL, description/README keywords. A project can have several formats. Tightened 2026-09-18: bare 'pipeline', 'paper', 'journal' and generic docs/site folders no longer trigger the pipeline, paper and GitHub-Pages formats.

readme_features._comment: Section/heading and content features (§17) matched case-insensitively on README text. 'headings' patterns are applied to markdown headings only; 'content' patterns to the whole text.

repo_archetypes._comment: Mutually exclusive archetypes assigned per data repository in this priority order (first rule that matches wins). Signals are derived fields computed by src/pipeline/build_supply.py. 'open_source_contribution' is not measurable with the collected fields (contributions to others' repositories are not fetched) and was removed 2026-09-18. Order changed 2026-09-18: ML/AI method themes are checked before production-style and data-engineering signals, so an ML repository with Docker/CI or a CV 'pipeline' stays an ML project.

evidence_rules._comment: Evidence strength for a capability per candidate (§10): 'mentioned' = word in bio only; 'used' = appears in repository language/topic/description of an owned non-fork repo; 'demonstrated' = appears in the README of a documented data project (README >= 1,000 chars) or is the primary language of such a project; 'project_demonstrated' = same and the project is not flagged educational; 'professional' = not observable on GitHub (company field is not evidence of the skill). Numbers here define thresholds.
evidence_rules.project_definition: owned (not fork), not archived, classified data repository, with a README of at least 300 characters OR at least 1 star OR a non-empty description; a bare repository without any of these is counted as 'repository' but not as 'project'.

data_user_tiers.T1_bio_declared: bio maps to a data role family (bio_role_overrides or Layer 1 title rules)
data_user_tiers.T2_repo_evidenced: not T1, and (>= 1 documented data project AND >= 2 data repositories) OR (>= 1 substantive project with >= 3 stars) — rule tightened 2026-09-18

certification_patterns._comment: Certification evidence in bios, repository names/descriptions and READMEs. Layer 1 config/skills_taxonomy.json 'certifications' patterns are applied as well; these add the candidate-side phrasings (capstone repos, badge names).

education_bio_patterns._comment: Education evidence in bios and READMEs (candidate side). Level and field lists mirror Layer 1 education entries so that DS08 can join on the same labels.

institutions._comment: Austrian institutions named in bios; used only to count institution mentions in aggregate, never to identify anyone.

cross_platform_domains._comment: Domains recognised in profile website/blog fields, social accounts and README links. Presence is counted per candidate; URLs themselves are stored only privately.

readme_skill_rules._comment: Layer 1 skill patterns were written for job advertisements; in README prose several generic entries over-fire. For README-derived evidence these skills use the stricter pattern below (replacing the Layer 1 pattern) and/or must match at least twice ('min2'). 'excluded' skills get no README/repo evidence at all: Git is true by construction on GitHub and is reported as such.

strict.Data Governance/Quality: data quality|data governance|data validation|great expectations|\bdbt test|data catalog|data lineage|\bdata steward|schema validation|\bpandera\b|\bpydantic\b
